definition: 2N Redundancy — a fault-tolerant design providing two independent, identical sets of critical infrastructure (2× capacity) for power or cooling; ensures full redundancy by allowing one entire system to fail or be taken offline for maintenance without impacting operations.
aliases: 2N; N+N; dual redundancy; fully redundant; 2N configuration

definition: Adiabatic Cooling — cooling technique that pre-cools air through evaporation of water (an adiabatic process) before it enters data center heat exchangers; this evaporation lowers the air temperature and reduces the need for mechanical chilling, improving energy efficiency.
aliases: adiabatic cooling; evaporative cooling; adiabatic cooling system; indirect evaporative cooling; evaporative cooling system

definition: Automatic Transfer Switch — an electrical switchgear device that automatically transfers the power supply from a primary source (utility) to a backup source (generator) when the primary source fails; ensures critical loads receive near-instantaneous power from generators during a utility outage.
aliases: automatic transfer switch; ATS; auto transfer switch; transfer switch; backup power switch

definition: Cabinet — an enclosed server rack with doors and side panels, used to secure and organize IT equipment; provides the same 19-inch rack mounting rails as an open rack, but offers additional security, airflow control, and containment of hot exhaust and cold intake air.
aliases: server cabinet; IT cabinet; rack cabinet; enclosed rack; equipment cabinet

definition: Chiller — an industrial cooling system component that removes heat from water via a refrigeration cycle, producing chilled water for air conditioning; in data centers, chillers supply cold water to CRAH units or cooling coils, which then cool the air circulating through IT equipment.
aliases: chiller; water chiller; chilled water unit; chiller unit; chiller system

definition: Colocation — practice of renting space for servers and other IT hardware in a third-party data center facility; the provider supplies power, cooling, connectivity, and security, while the customer owns and manages the equipment.
aliases: colo; co-location; colocation facility; multi-tenant data center; colocation hosting

definition: Heat rejection device that dissipates waste heat from a water-cooled chiller system to the atmosphere.
aliases: cooling towers; CT; evaporative cooling tower

definition: Computer Room Air Conditioner — cooling unit using direct expansion (DX) refrigeration to control temperature and humidity in a data center; circulates chilled air to remove heat from IT equipment.
aliases: computer room air conditioner; CRAC unit; data center AC; DX cooling unit

definition: Computer Room Air Handler — cooling unit using chilled water and air handlers to regulate temperature and humidity in a data center; similar to a CRAC but uses a chilled water heat exchanger instead of a direct expansion cycle.
aliases: computer room air handler; CRAH unit; chilled water air handler; CRAH cooling

definition: Cross Connect — a physical, point-to-point cable link that directly interconnects two different networks, carriers, or systems inside a data center; usually provisioned in a meet-me room or main distribution area to enable secure, low-latency connections between parties.
aliases: cross connect; cross-connect; cross connection; interconnect; interconnect cable

definition: A specialized facility designed to house computer systems, IT infrastructure, servers, storage arrays, and networking equipment. Data centers provide controlled environments with redundant power, cooling, and security systems to ensure 24/7 operations.
aliases: datacenter; DC; data centre; server farm; colocation facility; colo

definition: Data Center Infrastructure Management — software systems that monitor, manage, and optimize data center resources (power, cooling, space, and equipment); provides real-time visibility into operations, asset tracking, and capacity planning to improve efficiency and uptime.
aliases: data center infrastructure management; DCIM software; DCIM platform; data center management software; DCIM tool

definition: Data Center Infrastructure Efficiency — percentage measure of data center energy efficiency; defined as the ratio of IT equipment power to total data center power (inverse of PUE), where higher percentages indicate better efficiency.
aliases: data center infrastructure efficiency; DCIE; data center efficiency; DCiE metric

definition: Edge Computing — deploying data processing and storage resources at locations closer to end users or devices to reduce network latency and bandwidth usage; often involves small, distributed micro data centers for real-time processing and faster local response.
aliases: edge data center; edge site; micro data center; distributed edge; edge architecture

definition: Free Cooling — method of cooling a data center using naturally cool ambient air or water (from outside environment) to dissipate heat instead of relying solely on chillers or compressors; often implemented via air-side or water-side economizers to improve energy efficiency.
aliases: free cooling; economizer cooling; air-side economizer; water-side economizer; ambient cooling

definition: Hot Aisle/Cold Aisle — arrangement of server racks to separate hot exhaust air from cold intake air; ensures that equipment intakes receive cooled air while hot return air is isolated, improving overall cooling efficiency and preventing hot–cold air mixing.
aliases: hot aisle cold aisle; hot/cold aisle; hot aisle containment; cold aisle containment; aisle segregation

definition: Hyperscale — describes extremely large-scale data centers designed for cloud providers or major internet companies; characterized by thousands of servers and high-density infrastructure, enabling massive scalability to handle vast workloads for a global user base.
aliases: hyperscale data center; hyper-scale; mega data center; web-scale data center; cloud data center

definition: ISO 27001 — an international standard (ISO/IEC 27001) for establishing and maintaining an information security management system (ISMS); provides a systematic framework for managing sensitive data and security controls, and organizations (including data centers) seek ISO 27001 certification to validate their information security practices.
aliases: ISO 27001; ISO/IEC 27001; ISO 27001:2013; information security standard; ISMS standard

definition: Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design — a globally recognized green building certification system developed by the U.S. Green Building Council; data center facilities can earn LEED certification by meeting sustainability and efficiency criteria in design, construction, and operations.
aliases: LEED; LEED certification; green building certification; sustainable design; LEED rating

definition: Meet-Me Room — secure, centralized area in a data center where multiple telecommunications carriers and providers interconnect; contains demarcation equipment and cross-connects that allow tenants and networks to exchange data traffic directly within the facility.
aliases: meet-me room; MMR; meet me room; interconnect room; carrier room

definition: Mean Time Between Failures — a reliability metric indicating the average operating time between inherent failures of a system or component; typically measured in hours, it predicts how frequently an equipment or system is likely to fail during continuous operation.
aliases: mean time between failures; MTBF rate; reliability metric; failure interval; average uptime

definition: Mean Time to Repair — a maintainability metric measuring the average time required to diagnose and repair a failed component or system and restore it to normal operation; includes detection, troubleshooting, and fix time for the failure.
aliases: mean time to repair; MTTR rate; repair time; recovery time; fix time

definition: A redundancy configuration where the system has one additional (N+1) component beyond what is required for normal operation; allows maintenance or a single failure without downtime.
aliases: N + 1; N +1; N1+; N+1 redundancy; N plus 1

definition: Power Distribution Unit — an electrical device in a rack that distributes power to multiple pieces of IT equipment via multiple outlets; may be basic or "intelligent" (with remote monitoring and switching) and often includes circuit protection.
aliases: power distribution unit; rack PDU; cabinet PDU; power strip; power distribution strip

definition: Power Usage Effectiveness — ratio of total facility energy consumption to IT equipment energy consumption; a widely used data center efficiency metric where a value closer to 1.0 indicates greater energy efficiency.
aliases: power usage effectiveness; power utilization effectiveness; PUE ratio; PUE metric

definition: Raised Floor — elevated floor system in a data center that creates an under-floor plenum for distributing cooled air and for routing power and data cabling; facilitates efficient cooling airflow and organized cable management.
aliases: raised access floor; access floor; raised flooring; access flooring; raised floor system

definition: Recovery Point Objective — the maximum acceptable amount of data loss (measured in time) that can be tolerated after an interruption; defines how up-to-date data should be when restored (e.g. an RPO of 4 hours means backups or replicas at least every four hours).
aliases: recovery point objective; RPO window; acceptable data loss; backup interval; RPO target

definition: Recovery Time Objective — the maximum targeted duration of downtime after an outage within which systems must be restored; defines how quickly operations need to be resumed to avoid significant impact (e.g. an RTO of 2 hours means service must be back online within 2 hours).
aliases: recovery time objective; RTO window; downtime tolerance; restore time; RTO target

definition: Server Rack — standardized frame structure (typically 19-inch width) for mounting and organizing servers, network switches, and other IT equipment in a vertical stack; racks may be open-frame or enclosed (cabinet style) and are designed to support hardware while aiding airflow and cable management.
aliases: server rack; rack; equipment rack; 19-inch rack; open rack

definition: Service Level Agreement — contract between a service provider and a client that defines expected service standards (such as uptime, performance, support response) and how they are measured; typically includes uptime commitments (e.g. 99.99% availability) and remedies if those levels are not met.
aliases: service level agreement; SLA contract; uptime guarantee; service commitment; service contract

definition: Service Organization Control 2 — a compliance standard (developed by AICPA) for service organizations, which defines requirements for managing customer data across five trust service categories (security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, privacy); data center operators undergo regular SOC 2 audits to demonstrate strong security and operational controls.
aliases: SOC 2; Service Organization Control 2; SOC II; SOC Type 2; SOC audit

definition: Backup power capacity available to support critical loads during utility outage, typically supplied by diesel generators and UPS systems.
aliases: backup power; emergency power; generator backup; emergency generator; standby gen

definition: Tier I/II/III/IV — standardized data center classification defined by the Uptime Institute, ranging from Tier I (basic infrastructure) to Tier IV (fault-tolerant infrastructure with multiple redundancies); higher tiers correspond to increasing levels of redundancy and availability.
aliases: Tier 1; Tier 2; Tier 3; Tier 4; Uptime tiers

definition: Uninterruptible Power Supply — power conditioning and short-term energy storage between utility and generator.
aliases: uninterruptible power supply; battery UPS; static UPS; rotary UPS

definition: White Space — the area within a data center where IT equipment (servers, storage, networking) is housed; refers to the conditioned, secure space containing racks and cabinets (as opposed to mechanical or electrical support areas in the "gray space").
aliases: whitespace; white space area; data hall; IT floor space; technical space
